outcomes: Framework packages attach stable codes, attributes, categories, retryability, and source information to errors
Callers inspect semantic error information across wrapped and aggregated error trees
Client serialization exposes user and security messages while hiding internal details
Observability integrations receive structured creation events without creating package cycles
nonGoals: Defining every domain-specific error code in the core package
Using the JSON representation as a cross-service wire protocol

requirements.text: New and Bug capture a stack at the origin, while Wrap adds boundary meaning without capturing another stack and returns nil for a nil cause.
JSON and HTTP serialization expose messages and attributes only for user or security categories, omit stack and cause data, and substitute a generic internal message otherwise.
Code, attributes, category, and retryability remain discoverable through single-cause and multi-cause error trees.
Creation hooks are removable, panic-isolated, reentrancy-safe, and fire only when a new origin error or bug error is created.
